Cameras: 7 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Urbana's borders in OpenStreetMap (7 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022, as the village reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Champaign County and, unless the municipality has left it, the surrounding township.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($2,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: Ohio local candidates file campaign finance reports with their county board of elections, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
Cameras: no license-plate cameras are mapped inside Village of St. Paris's borders in OpenStreetMap as of 2026-10-20.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Ohio yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
